description: Golden Q/A for the demo corpus (Attention Is All You Need, arXiv 1706.03762). Ingest that paper before running retrieval eval.

cases.question: What is multi-head attention and why use multiple heads?
cases.reference_answer: Multi-head attention projects queries, keys, and values into several subspaces, runs attention in parallel, then concatenates the outputs so the model can jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.

cases.question: Why does the Transformer scale the dot products of queries and keys by the square root of the key dimension?
cases.reference_answer: Without scaling, large dot products push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps the variance of the dot products stable and improves training.

cases.question: How does the Transformer inject sequence order without recurrence?
cases.reference_answer: It adds positional encodings (sine and cosine functions of different frequencies) to the input embeddings so the model can use relative or absolute position information.

cases.question: In the Transformer encoder-decoder, what do the decoder queries attend to in the encoder-decoder attention layers?
cases.reference_answer: In encoder-decoder attention, queries come from the previous decoder layer while keys and values come from the encoder output, allowing every decoder position to attend over all encoder positions.
